//: Lighthouse CI against the STATIC build. Read this before adding an assertion.
The CI job serves dist/public with `serve -s`, whose documented behaviour is
'Rewrite all not-found requests to index.html'. The -s is there so client
routes like /fund and /apply load instead of 404ing, and it cannot be removed
without breaking them. It also means every /api/* request returns an HTML
document with status 200: the tRPC calls, the CSRF token, and crucially
/api/img, which is how every image on the homepage is served.
So in this environment the page's images are HTML files and its data calls
return markup. Anything downstream of that measures the harness, not the site.
That is why this job had been red on every recent main run while reporting
conclusion 'success': performance 0.35, LCP 15.1s and TTI 15.4s against a
LOCAL server, categories.best-practices null, and a failed `charset` audit for
a charset present both in client/index.html line 5 and on the live response.
A null category plus a failed deterministic audit is a degraded collection run.
What IS honest here is markup: accessibility and SEO are read from the DOM the
build actually produced. Those already passed while everything else failed,
which is the whole argument for this split.
The preset is deliberately NOT used. `lighthouse:no-pwa` asserts at error level
by default, so a Lighthouse version bump silently adds new gates: that is how
forced-reflow-insight, image-delivery-insight and network-dependency-tree-insight
started failing without anyone changing this file. Assert explicitly, so a new
audit is a decision rather than an upgrade side effect.
Measuring real performance needs a real server with a database and the image
proxy, which means auditing the deployed site rather than a static artifact.
That is a separate job and a separate decision, not something to fake here.
